territorial_scope.description: Applies across the United Kingdom, with the controls covering exports and electronic transfers to any destination.

evidence.quote: Regulations 1 and 2 extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

summary.short: Amends the UK Export Control Order 2008 and the assimilated Dual-Use Regulation (EC) 428/2009 control lists from 1 April 2024. Adds export and electronic-transfer prohibitions for emerging technologies, including advanced integrated circuits, cryogenic CMOS and quantum computers, and updates existing military and dual-use entries.
summary.long: The Export Control (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/346) were made on 7 March 2024 under sections 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 of the Export Control Act 2002 and Article 15(1) of Council Regulation (EC) No 428/2009. They come into force on 1 April 2024. Regulation 2 amends Schedule 2 (military goods) and Schedule 3 (UK controlled dual-use goods) of the Export Control Order 2008. It inserts new entries PL9013, PL9014 and PL9015. PL9013 covers cryogenic CMOS integrated circuits, dry-etching and SEM equipment, integrated circuits with a total processing performance of 6000 or more (including GPUs, TPUs and neural processors), parametric amplifiers, cryogenic cooling, EUV masks, and related software and technology. PL9014 covers quantum computers and computers containing PL9013.a.4 circuits. PL9015 covers metal additive manufacturing equipment and certain coating technology. For these items the export or transfer by electronic means is prohibited to any destination. Regulation 3 amends Annex I of Regulation 428/2009, changing definitions and control entries across the categories 1 to 9, including cryptography controls in 5A002. Regulations 1 and 2 extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland; Regulation 3 extends to England and Wales and Scotland. The text itself does not set penalties.}},

obligations.summary: Prohibits the export, or 'transfer by electronic means', to any destination of the listed goods, software and technology in new Schedule 3 entries PL9013 (cryogenic CMOS, dry-etching and SEM equipment, high-performance integrated circuits, cryogenic cooling, EUV masks, materials, software and technology), PL9014 (quantum computers and related items, and computers containing PL9013.a.4 integrated circuits) and PL9015 (metal additive manufacturing equipment and related software and technology, and coating technology). The prohibition applies to each listed item as worded in the entries.

evidence.provision: Reg. 2(3)(b) (inserting PL9013, PL9014 and PL9015 into Schedule 3 to the Export Control Order 2008)
evidence.quote: The export or “transfer by electronic means” of the following goods, “software” or “technology”, is prohibited to any destination:

entities.note: The text names no firms or facilities and designates or empowers no public authority. It names the Secretary of State (maker of the Regulations), the Department for Business and Trade (signing department) and the Export Control Joint Unit (holder of the Explanatory Memorandum), none of which is designated or empowered by this text.

enforcement.note: This amending regulation changes control-list entries in Schedules 2 and 3 to the Export Control Order 2008 and Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 428/2009. It creates no offence, fine, licence revocation or other sanction. Any enforcement provisions would sit in the parent Order, which this text does not reproduce.
